# New TunePad cell
# GAME MUSIC PROTOTYPE - DRUM TRACK
# This track creates the rhythmic structure for the composition.
# It is divided into Intro, Main, Build-up, Climax and Ending sections.

# Number of bars used for each main section
SECTION_BARS = 8


# ---------- INTRO ----------
def intro_bar():
    # Simple drum pattern used to introduce the rhythm gradually.
    # Kick drum and hi-hat start together.
    playNote([0, 4], beats=0.5)

    # Hi-hat continues on its own.
    playNote(4, beats=0.5)
    playNote(4, beats=0.5)

    # Snare and hi-hat play together to create a backbeat.
    playNote([2, 4], beats=0.5)

    # The same four-beat pattern is repeated to complete the bar.
    playNote([0, 4], beats=0.5)
    playNote(4, beats=0.5)
    playNote(4, beats=0.5)
    playNote([2, 4], beats=0.5)


# ---------- MAIN ----------
def main_bar():
    # The main section uses a stronger kick pattern
    # to make the rhythm feel more energetic than the intro.

    playNote([0, 4], beats=0.5)
    playNote(4, beats=0.5)

    # An extra kick is added here to strengthen the groove.
    playNote([0, 4], beats=0.5)

    # Snare and hi-hat create the main backbeat.
    playNote([2, 4], beats=0.5)

    # Repeat the same pattern for the second half of the bar.
    playNote([0, 4], beats=0.5)
    playNote(4, beats=0.5)
    playNote([0, 4], beats=0.5)
    playNote([2, 4], beats=0.5)


# ---------- BUILD-UP ----------
def build_up_bar():
    # The build-up divides the bar into 16 shorter rhythmic steps.
    # Shorter beat values make the rhythm feel faster and more intense.
    for step in range(16):

        # Start every step with a hi-hat.
        notes = [4]

        # Add kick drums at the beginning and middle of the pattern.
        if step == 0 or step == 8:
            notes.append(0)

        # Add snare drums at selected strong beats.
        if step == 4 or step == 12:
            notes.append(2)

        # Each step lasts 0.25 beats, creating a denser rhythm.
        playNote(notes, beats=0.25)


# ---------- CLIMAX ----------
def climax_bar(first_bar=False):
    # The climax uses a denser and more active drum pattern.
    # The parameter "first_bar" is used to add a crash cymbal
    # only at the beginning of the climax section.

    for step in range(16):

        # Hi-hat plays continuously to maintain energy.
        notes = [4]

        # More kick positions are added to create a stronger groove.
        if step in [0, 6, 8, 14]:
            notes.append(0)

        # Snare keeps the backbeat in the climax.
        if step in [4, 12]:
            notes.append(2)

        # Add a crash cymbal only on the first step
        # of the first climax bar.
        if first_bar and step == 0:
            notes.append(9)

        # Short note duration keeps the climax fast and energetic.
        playNote(notes, beats=0.25)


# ---------- ENDING ----------
def ending():
    # Reuse the intro rhythm to reduce the intensity
    # and create a clearer ending section.
    for i in range(3):
        intro_bar()

    # Final sequence uses kick, hi-hat, snare and crash
    # to clearly finish the composition.
    playNote([0, 9], beats=1)
    playNote(4, beats=1)
    playNote(2, beats=1)
    playNote(9, beats=1)


# ---------- FULL STRUCTURE ----------
# The functions below are arranged in sequence
# to create the complete drum composition.

# Intro section
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    intro_bar()

# Main section
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    main_bar()

# Build-up section
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    build_up_bar()

# Climax section
# "first_bar" is True only for the first repetition,
# so the crash cymbal is not repeated every bar.
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    climax_bar(first_bar=(i == 0))

# Ending section
ending()

# New TunePad cell
# GAME MUSIC PROTOTYPE - BASS TRACK
# This track supports the drum and piano melody.
# It adds low-frequency energy and follows the same
# Intro, Main, Build-up, Climax and Ending structure.

SECTION_BARS = 8

# Root notes for the bass progression:
# D -> Bb -> F -> C
bass_roots = [38, 34, 41, 36]


# ---------- INTRO ----------
def intro_bass():
    # The intro uses longer bass notes
    # to create a simple and spacious beginning.
    for root in bass_roots:
        playNote(root, beats=1)


# ---------- MAIN ----------
def main_bass():
    # The main section uses the same bass progression
    # but with shorter notes to create more movement.
    for root in bass_roots:
        playNote(root, beats=0.5)
        playNote(root, beats=0.5)


# ---------- BUILD-UP ----------
def build_up_bass():
    # The build-up repeats each bass note more frequently
    # to increase rhythmic energy.
    for root in bass_roots:
        for i in range(4):
            playNote(root, beats=0.25)


# ---------- CLIMAX ----------
def climax_bass():
    # The climax uses a more active bass pattern.
    # Higher octave notes are mixed with the root notes
    # to make the section feel stronger.
    for root in bass_roots:

        pattern = [
            root,
            root,
            root + 12,
            root
        ]

        for note in pattern:
            playNote(note, beats=0.25)


# ---------- ENDING ----------
def ending_bass():
    # The ending returns to longer notes
    # to reduce the energy before the final note.
    for i in range(3):
        for root in bass_roots:
            playNote(root, beats=1)

    # Final D bass note held for four beats.
    playNote(38, beats=4)


# ---------- FULL STRUCTURE ----------

# Intro
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    intro_bass()

# Main
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    main_bass()

# Build-up
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    build_up_bass()

# Climax
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    climax_bass()

# Ending
ending_bass()

# New TunePad cell
# GAME MUSIC PROTOTYPE - PIANO MELODY TRACK
# This track creates the main melody of the composition.
# It follows the same structure as the drum and bass tracks:
# Intro, Main, Build-up, Climax and Ending.

SECTION_BARS = 8


# Main note patterns used in different sections
intro_notes = [62, 65, 69, 65]
main_notes = [62, 65, 69, 72, 69, 67, 65, 62]
build_up_notes = [62, 65, 67, 69, 72, 74, 72, 69]
climax_notes = [74, 72, 69, 72, 74, 77, 76, 74]


# ---------- INTRO ----------
def intro_melody():
    # The intro uses fewer and longer notes
    # to create a simple atmospheric beginning.
    for note in intro_notes:
        playNote(note, beats=1)


# ---------- MAIN ----------
def main_melody():
    # The main section introduces a more complete melody.
    # Shorter notes create more movement.
    for note in main_notes:
        playNote(note, beats=0.5)


# ---------- BUILD-UP ----------
def build_up_melody():
    # The melody gradually moves upward in pitch
    # to create tension before the climax.
    for note in build_up_notes:
        playNote(note, beats=0.5)


# ---------- CLIMAX ----------
def climax_melody():
    # The climax uses higher notes and stronger velocity
    # to create the most energetic section.
    for note in climax_notes:
        playNote(note, beats=0.5, velocity=105)


# ---------- ENDING ----------
def ending_melody():
    # A descending melody reduces the energy
    # after the climax.
    ending_notes = [69, 67, 65, 62]

    # Repeat the descending phrase three times.
    # 4 notes x 3 repetitions x 1 beat = 12 beats.
    for i in range(3):
        for note in ending_notes:
            playNote(note, beats=1)

    # Hold the final D note for four beats.
    # Ending total = 12 + 4 = 16 beats.
    playNote(62, beats=4)


# ---------- FULL STRUCTURE ----------

# Intro:
# 4 beats per melody x 8 = 32 beats
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    intro_melody()

# Main:
# 4 beats per melody x 8 = 32 beats
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    main_melody()

# Build-up:
# 4 beats per melody x 8 = 32 beats
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    build_up_melody()

# Climax:
# 4 beats per melody x 8 = 32 beats
for i in range(SECTION_BARS):
    climax_melody()

# Ending:
# 16 beats
ending_melody()
